analysis:
Announcing the Lakhpati Didi initiative from the Red Fort on 15 August 2023, the Prime Minister set a target of two crore Lakhpati Didis — women in self-help groups with an annual household income of at least ₹1 lakh.

PIB material for the interim Budget of 1 February 2024 recorded that nearly one crore women had already become Lakhpati Didis, and raised the target to three crore. DD India reported that 1.48 crore women had reached the status by June 2025. The official Lakhpati Didi dashboard shows 3.46 crore Lakhpati Didis against 6.21 crore potential Lakhpati Didis.

On these figures the original two-crore target set in August 2023 was crossed, and a new target of six crore by 2029-30 has since been announced.
notes: No explicit deadline was stated in the 15 August 2023 announcement, so 'deadline' is null; the claim is scored on the two-crore target. The speech was in Hindi and quote_english is the widely reported English wording. The dashboard figure (3.46 crore) reflects the government's own count and is not independently audited. The 'nearly 1 crore by Feb 2024' and '3.46 crore by 2026' figures are large; definitions (annual household income of ₹1 lakh) are set by the scheme.
